subtype: Approach: fixed meeting point agreed in advance [Action]
passage: Come, sit, and I will tell you about the day your cousin Kiran got lost at the fair. Before we went in, I told the boy, "If we lose each other, come to the temple gate. Do not wander." Then, near the sweet stalls, the crowd pushed us apart. I stood at the gate with my heart in my mouth, staring at every small head. And there he came, marching straight from the lane, with a shopkeeper pointing the way behind him. I am Aadhya, his aunt, and I have never been so glad to see a proud face. He had not cried once. The plan had told him where to go.

qa.q: Where had Aadhya and Kiran agreed to meet if they lost each other?
qa.a: They agreed to meet at the temple gate.

qa.q: What was Aadhya feeling as she waited at the gate?
qa.a: Worried, with her heart in her mouth, and then very glad when Kiran appeared.

qa.q: What choice did Kiran make that kept him safe?
qa.a: He went straight to the agreed place and let a shopkeeper point the way, instead of wandering about.

qa.q: How did Kiran see the plan Aadhya had given him?
qa.a: He trusted it, since the plan told him where to go and let him get there without crying.

grounding: A family agrees a meeting point beforehand, so the lost child walks straight to it with a shopkeeper's directions.

subtype: Approach: fixed meeting point agreed in advance [Action]
passage: Before the Rath Yatra crowd, Salma Phuppo had squeezed Pranav's shoulder. "If we get separated, meet me at the temple gate. The big one with the elephants." An hour later, in the pushing, singing crowd, Pranav lost her. Then the rain started, sheets of it, and everyone ran for cover. Pranav couldn't see the temple at all. His stomach flipped. But he knew exactly where he needed to be. He went into a sweet shop with its shutters half down and asked the owner, "Which way is the temple gate with the elephants?" The man pointed. "Straight, then left at the post box." Pranav walked, soaked, counting streets. At the gate, under the stone elephants, Phuppo was waiting, dripping and smiling.

qa.q: What did the temple gate have on it?
How did Pranav feel when he couldn't see the temple in the rain?
qa.a: He felt a flash of fear, his stomach flipping, but steadier once he remembered the meeting point.

qa.q: What else could the family add to the plan for next time?
qa.a: They could add a phone number for Pranav to give a shopkeeper, in case he can't reach the gate.

qa.q: How does the meeting point look to Salma Phuppo?
qa.a: Phuppo knows exactly where to wait, so she can stay calm even in the rain until Pranav arrives.

grounding: It shows a child who, after being separated, walks straight to an agreed temple-gate meeting point with a shopkeeper's directions and finds his aunt waiting.

subtype: Approach: fixed meeting point agreed in advance [Action]
passage: On Sunday Shankar and his aunt Sudha went to the flower market near the Mylapore temple. At the entrance she had pointed to the temple's tall painted gate. "If you lose me, go there and wait." Twenty minutes later, as a lorry of marigolds unloaded and the crowd surged, Shankar found himself alone. He didn't search the lanes. He looked up. The top of the painted gate showed over the stalls, but the lanes twisted. He asked a woman at a fixed flower stall, "How do I get to the temple gate?" She pointed. "Keep the lamp shop on your right." Shankar walked, not running, until the gate was in front of him. Sudha Chithi was already there, arms folded, smiling.

qa.q: What was being unloaded when the crowd surged?
How did Shankar feel once he knew where to go?
qa.a: He felt steady and sure of what to do, walking calmly instead of running.

qa.q: What else could Shankar do if the gate was crowded and he couldn't see his aunt?
qa.a: He could stand at one side of the gate and wait there, or ask a shopkeeper nearby to call Sudha Chithi's number.

qa.q: How does the meeting point plan look to Sudha Chithi?
qa.a: Sudha Chithi can wait calmly at the gate knowing Shankar will head there, so she feels relieved when he arrives.

grounding: It shows a child walking straight to the meeting point his family agreed on, with a stall-keeper's directions, and finding his aunt waiting.
